'''Brok Ziam''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who lived on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. He was the Director of Operations of the [[White Thranta Shipping Company]], a front for the illegal activities of [[Jabba's criminal empire/Legends|Jabba the Hutt's criminal organization]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|I need this place to make some cash. I'm going to need plenty to fight off Jabba after I take over his hold on this place. I'm sure he's going to want it back bad enough to send a lot of his men. I need to be ready.|Brok Ziam's journal|<ref name="SWG:SO" />}}
By the time of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], members of the White Thranta Shipping under Brok Ziam got involved in questionable medical activities. They performed unethical experiments on sapient races in the bunker bellow the [[White Thranta Shipping offices]],<ref name="SWG:DP">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Data Purge|Tatooine}}</ref> without [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]] being aware of it.<ref name="SWG:JDW">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=other}}Legacy Quest: "Jabba's Dirty Work" on Tatooine</ref> Ziam's plan was to use the White Thranta Shipping Company to make enough money to eventually break away from Jabba.<ref name="SWG:DI">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Digital Infection|Tatooine}}</ref> In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline" /> Jabba's employee [[Reimos Taligg]] tasked a spacer to slice the computers of the White Thranta bunker, eventually discovering the situation.<ref name="SWG:DI" /> Reimos then requested the spacer to question Brok Ziam but Ziam refused, forcing the spacer to kill him.<ref name="SWG:SO" />

==Behind the scenes==
Brok Ziam was a [[Wikipedia:Non-player character|non-player character]] in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'', a [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online roleplaying game]] developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]],<ref name="SWG:SO" /> prior to its closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]].<ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref> Brok Ziam was added to the game as part of the "[[W:c:swg:Legacy Quest|Legacy Quest]]" with the release of the "[[W:c:swg:Publish 25 Notes for November 15, 2005|Publish 25]]," a.k.a. the "[[W:c:swg:New Game Enhancements|New Game Enhancements]]," on [[November 15]], [[2005]].<ref name="SonyCite-Publish Archive 2005">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=64886&resource=publish|text=Publish Archive 2005}}</ref>

In the game, Brok used to have the extended last name, Ziamzun.<ref name="SWG:SO" /><ref name="SWGTCGPOGG">[[Star Wars Galaxies: The Complete Guide: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Galaxies: The Complete Guide'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> For some unknown reason, the developers shortened the name '''Brok Ziamzun''' to Brok Ziam in the "[[:w:c:swg:Chapter 2|Chapter 2]]" update, released on [[August 1]], [[2006]].<ref name="SonyForumsCite-Chapter 2: The Talus Incident Publish Notes, August 1st">{{SonyForumsCite|full_url=http://soe.lithium.com/swg/board/message?board.id=DevDiscussion&message.id=58871|text="Chapter 2: The Talus Incident" Publish Notes, August 1st}}</ref> Furthermore, the Mos Eisley section of the "Legacy Quest" was revamped upon the release of the "[[:w:c:swg:Chapter 3|Chapter 3]]" update, on [[September 27]], 2006,<ref name="SonyCite-Chapter Archive 2006">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=64186&resource=publish|text=Chapter Archive 2006}}</ref> and Brok Ziam's quest was strongly modified, though the story line remained similar.<ref name="SWG:SO" />
